📚 Present Perfect · Grammar Basics

Why? We use Present Perfect to talk about actions that happened in the past but are still important NOW.

Form: have / has + past participle

✅ Affirmative & Negative Forms

Subject+ Affirmative− Negative
I / You / We / They I've baked a cake. I haven't baked a cake.
He / She / It He's eaten the apples. He hasn't eaten the apples.

Note: 've = have, 's = has, haven't = have not, hasn't = has not

🍳 Real Examples (Kitchen Edition)

Regular verbs: baked, washed, chopped, added

✓ "I've washed the cup."

✗ "I haven't washed the plate yet."

Irregular verbs: eaten, drunk, broken, made

✓ "She's eaten the apples."

✗ "They haven't made the cake."
